items.note: The page carries out the whole signed Kronecker substitution at B_0=2^{4p}: packing, four products of absolute values by the established multiplier, centered extraction, combination, wrapping mod y^r+1, truncation to Q_p(fg/r), and the cost total. It follows the paper's proof of Lemma lem:signed-ring-product closely. The only part it leaves out is the output-format step.

"Write f=2^{-p}(a+ib) and g=2^{-p}(c+ie), where a,b,c,e ... are integer-coefficient polynomials of degree below r with coefficients of absolute value at most 2^p. Set B_0=2^{4p}". This matches the paper, and the disk-grid hypothesis is restated as Gaussian-integer numerators of modulus at most 2^p.

"By the geometric sum, |A_u|<=2^p(B_0^r-1)/(B_0-1)<B_0^r/2, so its magnitude fits in 4pr bits." The first inequality is justified, as in the paper. The second strict inequality is asserted without the arithmetic, as the paper also does.

The page explains why absolute values are multiplied ("The multiplier takes nonnegative integers"), restores signs, and writes A_aA_c=(ac)(B_0)=sum_{j<2r} h_j B_0^j with the padding h_{2r-1}=0, matching the paper. The other three products are covered by the generic "Take a product integer Z".

dropped: hypothesis p >= 2, which the strict inequality 2^{3p} < B_0/2 = 2^{4p-1} requires
items.note: "Each h_j sums at most r products of coefficients of size at most 2^p, so |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2". The first inequality is spelled out, and the second rests on the earlier "Assume r<2^p". The third is not explained, and it needs p>=2, which the page never states.

The page gives the carry recurrence d_j, gamma_{j+1}, the bound -B_0<u_j+gamma_j<B_0 keeping the carry in {-1,0}, the telescoped identity A_u=sum d_jB_0^j+gamma_rB_0^r, and the sign test on gamma_r, as in the paper. It also verifies that complement-and-increment yields B_0^r-(A_u+B_0^r)=|A_u|.

The page defines q_j, epsilon, rho_j and the centered residue, and gives the carry in {0,1} from q_j+rho_j in [0,B_0]. It then proves widehat h_j=h_j by induction via sum_{i<j} q_iB_0^i = sum_{i<j} h_iB_0^i + rho_jB_0^j, the congruence, and the separation bound. This is the paper's residual-identity induction in slightly different form. The page asserts |Z|<B_0^{2r}/4 without citing the evaluation bound, and it compresses the use of the two representations of Z into "so"; both are correct.

"The real and imaginary numerator streams are ac-be and ae+bc. Since y^{j+r}=-y^j, reduce modulo y^r+1 by subtracting the coefficient at j+r from the one at j for 0<=j<r". This matches the paper and gives the reason for the wrap. The missing top coefficient is handled by the earlier padding h_{2r-1}=0.

The page uses the paper's counting argument: for each j_1, exactly one j_2 has j_1+j_2 ≡ j (mod r), with sign + or -. This gives a sum of exactly r signed products, so |H_j|<=r2^{2p}. From this it reads off that each coefficient 2^{-2p}H_j/r of fg/r has modulus at most 1, which is the specialization of the paper's ||fg/r||_inf <= ||f||_inf ||g||_inf.

items.note: The page derives the truncation (right shift by p+log_2 r), the error bound ("Each part loses less than 2^{-p}, so the error is less than sqrt2 2^{-p}"), and the cost: each multiplier input has at most 4pr bits, and every other stage is linear scans. It does not show that the returned truncated polynomial is still a disk grid polynomial, and it omits the output-format step.

errors.problem: The paper's hypotheses are r=2^ℓ<2^p with ℓ>=1 and p>=2. The page drops p>=2, which the chain r2^{2p}<2^{3p}<B_0/2 needs (2^{3p}<2^{4p-1} only for p>=2). It also never states that r is a power of two, which the later right shift by p+log_2 r needs.

errors.quote: A product is negative when exactly one operand is.
errors.problem: This is false when the other operand is zero, because then the product is 0. The sign rule is the product of the operand signs, as in the paper's "restore each product's sign".
